name: Contradictory Account State
problem: What the AI says about the person's own account (which quests exist, what changed, whether a change ran) is re-derived each turn from whatever slice it read, and a change it made is not read back, so within one session it can report the same state two ways, repeat a change it already made, or propose again what it said was done.
who_has_it: People who ask the AI to change their quests and then ask what state they are in.
why_it_matters: In production one account's quests were described as a single completed goal and then as four initialised quests within ten minutes, and the person asked what state the account was in four separate times. An assistant that cannot report its own state is hard to trust with changing it.
why_hard: The host's data changes from many places (the app, other people, background work), a card or cache of it lags, a read on every turn costs time, and a library that serves any host cannot assume one data model.
existing_attempts: A managed card per quest rebuilt on sync, through which a turn is grounded in its quest; live reads through the host's retrieval adapter; the quest change executor and its final-state metric; the answer check that flags claims of unexecuted work.

name: Different Science Evidence In Two Chats
problem: One science question can get different evidence in Quest chat than in Quest's research chat.
who_has_it: People who ask science questions in Quest chat and in the research chat, and the maintainers who keep both current.
why_it_matters: Two searches mean two sets of sources and two ways of weighing them, so the same question can get different advice, and an improvement to one has to be made again in the other.
why_hard: The research chat's search belongs to the research interface and the evidence service behind the Quest backend, QAR reaches a host's research sources only through declared interfaces, and a host's research search reaches a run only as a retrieval source or a custom tool.
existing_attempts: Web research that reads snippets and then pages, with an answer check that flags claims the turn's reads do not support; a host's research search offered to a run as a retrieval source or a custom tool.

name: Unrequested Or Partial Changes
problem: A request to change a quest leads to changes that were not asked for, to only part of what was asked, or to the same change made twice.
who_has_it: People and teammates who let the AI edit goals, notes and experiments for them.
why_it_matters: Quest data is the person's own plan. An unrequested write is hard to notice and undo, and a partial change leaves the plan inconsistent while the reply claims success.
why_hard: A change request is natural language mapped onto many tools with many arguments; a model tends to be helpful beyond the ask, multi-step requests need each step done once, and a retry after a timeout can repeat a write.
existing_attempts: Tool schemas with explicit arguments, a confirmation step for destructive actions, a scoped writer that performs only the one named operation, and database-level checks of the final state.
